records.stepTherapy: Class-wide PDL non-preferred PA criteria (not a strict step-therapy fail-first rule): a client must meet at least one of the following to get a non-preferred SSRI approved -- non-preferred drug usage prior to inpatient facility discharge, stability on the non-preferred drug, complication risk from switching off the non-preferred drug, documented treatment failure with preferred drugs within any subclass, contraindication or allergic reaction to preferred drugs, or treatment of stage-four advanced/metastatic cancer and associated conditions.
records.tier: PDL preferred (fee-for-service Medicaid; no dollar copay tiers -- 'preferred' means dispensed without PDL prior authorization)
records.verificationNote: Fetched the cited PDF directly (a plain curl/WebFetch on this URL returned HTTP 403; the file was retrieved via an authenticated browser session that resolved with HTTP 200, reassembled from base64 chunks, and validated as a genuine 88-page PDF matching the source's own page count). Page 1 confirms the document title 'Preferred Drug List -- Texas Health and Human Services -- Texas Medicaid, Effective July 24, 2026' and the table of contents (page 5) lists 'ANTIDEPRESSANTS, SSRIs' at page 22, matching the task's supplied source and effective date. Page 22's 'ANTIDEPRESSANTS, SSRIs' section was read verbatim: the PREFERRED AGENTS column lists citalopram tablets/solution, escitalopram tablets, fluoxetine capsules/solution, fluvoxamine, Lexapro (escitalopram), paroxetine (Paxil-equivalent generic), Prozac (fluoxetine), and sertraline concentration/tablets plus the Zoloft brand of the same; the NON-PREFERRED AGENTS column lists Celexa (citalopram brand), citalopram 30mg capsules, escitalopram capsules/solution, fluoxetine DR capsules, fluoxetine tablets, fluvoxamine ER, paroxetine (Brisdelle), paroxetine CR, Paxil, Paxil CR, and sertraline capsules. The page-level PA CRITERIA block (client must meet at least one of six listed conditions to get a non-preferred SSRI approved) was read verbatim and is transcribed into stepTherapy. Page 3 confirms non-preferred PDL status itself triggers PDL prior authorization ('Drugs identified as non-preferred require a PDL prior authorization'). All six SSRI molecules (citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, sertraline) are on the preferred list in at least one common oral form, with no restriction on the preferred form itself. Sertraline (tablet form) was selected as the representative single preferred agent because it is the most broadly first-line-prescribed generic SSRI in clinical practice, matching this repo's established ssri-oral convention across every other payer already gathered (VA Medicaid FFS, MD payers, etc.) -- this single-agent selection among five/six clinically-tied, equally-unrestricted SSRIs is an inference, not something the source itself ranks. The 50 mg strength and once-daily sig are standard prescribing convention, not stated in the PDL (which lists drug/formulation names and preferred/non-preferred status only, no dosing guidance). No quantity-limit or clinical-PA codes are shown in this class's table (unlike some other states' PDLs), so preferredRestriction is null.

records.verificationNote: Fetched the BCBS Texas Performance Drug List PDF directly (WebFetch's AI summarizer could not parse the compressed PDF text stream, but it saved the raw 3.07MB PDF file to a local path -- per the project's known 'looks dead but isn't' pattern, opened that saved file directly with a local PDF library instead of re-fetching). Cover page confirms title 'Performance Drug List, July 2026', publisher line '41722-T TX (c) Prime Therapeutics LLC 07/26', and every page header reads '2026 Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Texas July 2026 Performance Drug List', matching this exact payer (BCBS Texas commercial, PBM Prime Therapeutics). Read the legend on printed pages I-VI (PDF page indices 1-6, 'How to use this list' and 'Coverage considerations' sections): lower-case bold 'p' = Preferred Generic (Tier 1), lower-case 'np' = Non-Preferred Generic (Tier 2), CAPS 'P' = Preferred Brand (Tier 3), CAPS 'NP' = Non-Preferred Brand (Tier 4); 'PA'/'ST'/'QL' in the Requirements/Limits column flag prior authorization, step therapy, and quantity limits respectively, defined on printed page IV. Read the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM DRUGS > ANTIDEPRESSANTS section verbatim on printed pages 46-47 (PDF page indices 55-56). Confirmed exactly as listed: citalopram hydrobromide tab 10/20/40mg (Celexa) = p; citalopram oral soln 10mg/5ml = np; escitalopram oxalate tab 5/10/20mg (Lexapro) = p; escitalopram oxalate soln 5mg/5ml = np; fluoxetine hcl cap 10/20/40mg (Prozac) = p; fluoxetine hcl tab 10mg = p; fluoxetine hcl tab 20mg = np; fluoxetine hcl solution 20mg/5ml = np; FLUOXETINE DR (delayed-release cap 90mg) = NP, ST; fluvoxamine maleate tab 25/50mg = p; fluvoxamine maleate tab 100mg = np; paroxetine hcl tab 10/20/30/40mg (Paxil) = p; sertraline hcl tab 25/50/100mg (Zoloft) = p; sertraline hcl oral concentrate 20mg/ml = np. No PA, ST, or QL notation appears next to any of the six 'p' (Tier 1) oral SSRI entries, so none of them carries a preferred-agent restriction and there is no class-wide step-therapy criterion for the standard tablet/capsule forms. Preferred agent chosen as sertraline (most commonly prescribed first-line SSRI per standard clinical guidelines, matching the convention used for other payers in this dataset); citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, paroxetine, and fluvoxamine are all equally Tier 1 preferred per the source and listed as alternatives, since the document does not single out one SSRI over another. Dose/sig (sertraline 50mg once daily) is standard first-line dosing convention, not itself stated in the drug list (which lists drug names, tier letters, and Requirements/Limits only, no sig text). The document states member payment tiers as a description (up to six tiers: Preferred Generic/Non-Preferred Generic/Preferred Brand/Non-Preferred Brand/Preferred Specialty/Non-Preferred Specialty) but does not publish dollar copay amounts in this PDF, consistent with 'tier' reflecting the letter-coded tier only.

records.verificationNote: Read directly from the 'Humana Premier Rx Plan (PDP) Formulary 26402' 2026 Prescription Drug Guide (Y0040_PDG26_FINAL_5C_C 20260005PDG2640226C_v15), cover page states 'Updated 08/01/2026'. The Antidepressants section spans pages 22-23 of the PDF (labeled '2026 HUMANA FORMULARY UPDATED 08/01/2026'), which lists all six named SSRI generics (citalopram, escitalopram oxalate, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine hcl, sertraline) with exact tier numbers and utilization-management codes (MO/QL only -- no PA or ST flags on any dosage form of any of the six generics). Confirmed: sertraline tablet (25/50/100 mg), citalopram tablet, escitalopram tablet, and fluoxetine capsule are all Tier 1 - Preferred Generic (definition read from page 5: 'Generic or brand drugs that are available at the lowest cost share for the plan'); paroxetine tablet and fluvoxamine tablet are Tier 2 - Generic; less-common dosage forms (solutions, ER tablets, capsules of escitalopram/paroxetine) sit at Tier 3 or Tier 4. Sertraline 50 mg tablet was picked as the single preferred agent to match this app's convention (see ny-medicaid-ssris) since the document itself does not single out one SSRI over the others -- all four Tier-1 generics are equally 'preferred' by tier placement. The paRequired brand-name entries (Zoloft, Prozac, Celexa, Lexapro, Paxil, Luvox) are an inference, not an explicit non-formulary listing: full-text search of all 108 PDF pages confirmed none of those six brand names appear anywhere in the document, and this Humana guide is framed as an exhaustive 'list of covered drugs' (page 10), so absence from that list means the brand is not covered absent a formulary exception -- standard for a Part D plan once an AB-rated generic exists. No class-wide step-therapy criterion for SSRIs was found anywhere in the document.
